name: Web Application & API Fuzzing
description: Automated discovery of web application and API vulnerabilities through targeted fuzzing. Covers directory and path brute-forcing (ffuf, feroxbuster), parameter and header fuzzing, authentication-aware fuzzing with session management, OpenAPI/GraphQL schema-based API fuzzing, server-side template injection discovery, business logic fuzzing through input permutation, and integration of web fuzzing into assessment workflows.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to web application or API fuzzing

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands web fuzzing concepts and common tools
evidence: Can explain the difference between web fuzzing and binary/protocol fuzzing
Familiar with ffuf, Burp Intruder, and feroxbuster at a conceptual level
Understands wordlist selection and response filtering for web fuzzing
Completed introductory training on web application fuzzing

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Runs web fuzzing tools with provided configurations under supervision
evidence: Used ffuf for directory discovery and parameter brute-forcing in lab
Applied Burp Intruder with position markers and payload lists under guidance
Filtered fuzzing results by response code, size, and content to identify findings
Work reviewed by authorized tester

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently develops web fuzzing strategies tailored to target applications
evidence: Independently applied web fuzzing in 5+ web application assessments
Develops custom wordlists and fuzzing strategies based on application technology stack
Performs authentication-aware fuzzing maintaining session state across requests
Identifies injection points, hidden endpoints, and access control gaps through fuzzing

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Builds API schema-aware fuzzers; discovers complex vulnerabilities
evidence: Develops schema-based fuzzers from OpenAPI, GraphQL, and gRPC definitions
Builds custom fuzzing tools for application-specific logic and workflow testing
Chains fuzzing discoveries into exploitation (SSTI, SSRF, deserialization)
Mentors team on web fuzzing methodology and custom tool development

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on web fuzzing; develops methodology and discovers significant vulnerabilities
evidence: Discovered significant vulnerabilities in production web applications through fuzzing
Published research on web or API fuzzing techniques
Developed or maintains the lab's web fuzzing methodology and tool configurations
Trains teams on advanced web application fuzzing strategies

assessment_methods.description: Given a web application with hidden endpoints and injection points, use fuzzing techniques to discover vulnerabilities and document findings
Review of web fuzzing methodology, custom wordlists, and vulnerability findings from recent assessments
